# Starter (TypeScript)

Welcome to your fresh **[Robo.js](https://robojs.dev)** project!

Build, deploy, and maintain your Discord bots with ease. With Robo.js as your guide, you'll experience a seamless, [file-based setup](/docs/discord-bots/file-structure), an [integrated database](/docs/framework/core/flashcore), [TypeScript support](/docs/framework/core/typescript), and a multitude of [plugin-powered skills](/docs/plugins) to unlock along the way.

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/discord-bots" title="Documentation" description="Getting started with Robo.js" />
  <Card href="https://robojs.dev/discord" title="Discord" description="Robo - Imagine Magic" />
</Cards>

## Getting Started

Create a project with this template:

```package-install
npx create-robo <project-name> --template discord-bots/starter-ts
```

Then navigate into your project directory:

```bash
cd <project-name>
```

Run development mode:

```bash
npm run dev
```

## Development

Creating a **[Slash Command](/docs/discord-bots/commands)** is as easy as creating files.

<Files>
  <Folder name="src" defaultOpen disabled>
    <Folder name="commands" defaultOpen>
      <File name="ping.ts" note="/ping" />
    </Folder>
    <Folder name="context" defaultOpen>
      <Folder name="message" defaultOpen>
        <File name="Quote.ts" note="Message right-click" />
      </Folder>
    </Folder>
    <Folder name="events" defaultOpen>
      <File name="ready.ts" />
    </Folder>
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="config" defaultOpen disabled>
    <File name="robo.mjs" note="Main config" />
  </Folder>
  <File name=".env" />
</Files>

Let's say you want a new `/hello` command. Just create a file in the `/src/commands` directory named `hello.ts` and export a default function that returns something.

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```ts title="/src/commands/hello.ts"
    export default (interaction) => {
    	interaction.reply('Hello World!')
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="JavaScript">
    ```js title="/src/commands/hello.js"
    export default (interaction) => {
    	interaction.reply('Hello World!')
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Your `/hello` command is now ready to use! **Robo.js** takes care of registration for you.

Ever clicked on an avatar or message and seen an _Apps_ section? Those are **[Context Commands](/docs/discord-bots/context-menu)**!

Create a file in `/src/context/message` named after the command. For example, `Quote.ts`.

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```ts title="/src/context/message/Quote.ts"
    export default (interaction, message) => {
    	interaction.reply(`${message.author} said:\n\n> ${message.content}`)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="JavaScript">
    ```js title="/src/context/message/Quote.js"
    export default (interaction, message) => {
    	interaction.reply(`${message.author} said:\n\n> ${message.content}`)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Debugging

**Discord Bots** made with **Robo.js** come with a built-in **[Debugger](/docs/discord-bots/debug)**.

Whenever your bot crashes in development mode, the debugger shows an interactive error message - all within **Discord**!

You even get `/dev` **[Subcommands](/docs/discord-bots/commands#subcommands)** for quick access to logs, system info, and more. Just set your test server's ID as an **environment variable** called `DISCORD_GUILD_ID`.

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/discord-bots/debug" title="Debugging" description="Troubleshoot right within Discord." />
  <Card href="/docs/discord-bots/credentials#optional-variables" title="Credentials" description="Secure your Discord Bot credentials." />
</Cards>

## Client Configuration

**Robo.js** manages your **Discord.js** `Client` instance via the `@robojs/discordjs` plugin. Use `getClient()` to access it anywhere in your project.

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```ts
    import { getClient } from '@robojs/discordjs'

    export default () => {
    	const client = getClient()
    	return `My name is ${client.user.username}`
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="JavaScript">
    ```js
    import { getClient } from '@robojs/discordjs'

    export default () => {
    	const client = getClient()
    	return `My name is ${client.user.username}`
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Intents or other configurations can be set in the `config/plugins/robojs/discordjs.mjs` file.

```javascript title="/config/plugins/robojs/discordjs.mjs"
export default {
	clientOptions: {
		intents: ['Guilds', 'GuildMessages']
	}
}
```

## Robo Ecosystem

By building with **Robo.js**, you gain access to a growing ecosystem of **[plugins](/plugins)**, **[templates](/templates)**, and **[tools](/docs/robo-cli)**. **[Robo Plugins](/docs/plugins)** are special. They can add features with one command.

```bash
npx robo add @robojs/ai @robojs/moderation
```

Plugins integrate seamlessly thanks to the **[Robo File Structure](/docs/discord-bots/file-structure)**. What's more, anyone can **[create a plugin](/docs/framework/plugins/create)**.

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/framework/plugins/install" title="Robo Plugins" description="Add features to your Robo seamlessly." />
  <Card href="/docs/framework/plugins/create" title="Creating Plugins" description="Make your own plugins for Robo.js." />
</Cards>

## Hosting

**Hosting** your project keeps it running 24/7. No need to keep your computer on at all times, or worry about your Internet connection.

You can host on any platform that supports **Node.js**, or run `robo deploy` to host on **[RoboPlay](https://roboplay.dev)** - a hosting platform optimized for **Robo.js**.

```bash
npm run deploy
```
